name: exploratory semantic wrong-turn trigger analysis for one-step human BACK
interpretation: One-step human BACK is heterogeneous. When the immediately preceding click was a semantic wrong turn, the replacement branch is strongly corrective. When the preceding click already improved target-body similarity, the replacement is on average slightly worse than the abandoned page. This suggests that detecting wrong turns may be more important than encouraging BACK generically.
boundary: Post-hoc exploratory analysis; not a preregistered causal test.
Semantic similarity is a navigation proxy, not comprehension.
The result motivates a wrong-turn detector for later agent-assisted experiments but does not prove that humans explicitly monitor this semantic variable.
